kept.q: One major function of the wholesaler is 'breaking bulk'. What does this mean?
options: Buying goods directly from consumers
Transporting goods from one country to another
Advertising goods on behalf of manufacturers
Dividing large quantities of goods into smaller units for sale to retailers
kept.explanation: Breaking bulk means the wholesaler buys goods in large quantities from producers and divides them into smaller, manageable quantities that retailers can afford to buy and store.
kept.pidgin: Breaking bulk na when wholesaler buy plenty plenty goods from producer, then e go divide am into small small quantity wey retailer fit buy and keep.

kept.q: Which of the following is a service a wholesaler usually renders to retailers?
options: Granting credit facilities to retailers
Fixing the final selling price retailers must charge consumers
Manufacturing the goods they sell
Collecting value added tax on behalf of government
kept.explanation: Wholesalers often give retailers credit so they can stock goods and pay later after selling. This helps small retailers who may not have enough capital to pay cash immediately.
kept.pidgin: Wholesaler dey often give retailer credit make e fit carry goods first and pay later after e don sell am. Na im dey help small retailer wey no get enough money pay cash.

kept.q: A type of wholesaler whose customers, usually small retailers, must pay in cash and carry their own goods away without any home delivery service is called a ____ wholesaler.
options: Cash and carry
Mail order
Rack-jobber
Credit
kept.explanation: A cash and carry wholesaler sells goods only for cash and does not deliver; buyers must arrange their own transport to carry goods away. This keeps the wholesaler's operating cost low.
kept.pidgin: Cash and carry wholesaler na im be the one wey dey sell only for cash, e no dey deliver goods; na buyer go arrange how to carry im goods comot. Dis one dey make im cost low.

kept.q: Chief Nkemdirim, a wholesaler in Onitsha, bought 300 cartons of tomato paste at ₦12,000 per carton and later sold each carton to retailers at ₦17,000. What was his total profit on the 300 cartons?
kept.explanation: Profit per carton = 17,000 - 12,000 = 5,000. Total profit = 5,000 x 300 = 1,500,000. This shows how wholesalers earn their margin by buying in bulk and selling in smaller units at a higher price.
kept.pidgin: Profit for one carton = 17,000 minus 12,000 = 5,000. Total profit = 5,000 times 300 = 1,500,000. Na so wholesaler dey make profit, e dey buy plenty cheap, e dey sell small expensive.

kept.q: A manufacturer is most likely to bypass the wholesaler and sell directly to retailers or consumers in which of these situations?
options: When the manufacturer wants to store goods for very long periods before selling
When the manufacturer produces a small range of perishable goods that need quick delivery to the market
When the manufacturer produces goods in very large quantities for many retailers scattered across the country
When the manufacturer has no means of transport to move goods
kept.explanation: Perishable goods like fresh bread or milk spoil quickly, so manufacturers sell directly and fast to retailers or consumers to avoid delay and loss caused by passing through a wholesaler. Non-perishable goods meant for many scattered retailers usually still need a wholesaler.
kept.pidgin: Goods wey dey quick spoil like bread or fresh milk no get time to pass through wholesaler, so manufacturer go sell am sharp sharp direct to retailer or consumer make e no waste. Goods wey no dey spoil and wey plenty retailer dey scatter everywhere go still need wholesaler.

kept.q: A retailer bought an item from a wholesaler at a catalogue (list) price of ₦5,000 but was given a trade discount of 12%. How much did the retailer actually pay the wholesaler for the item?
kept.explanation: Trade discount = 12% of 5,000 = 600. Amount actually paid = 5,000 - 600 = 4,400. Trade discount is deducted from the catalogue price before the retailer pays, as a reward for buying from the wholesaler.
kept.pidgin: Trade discount = 12% of 5,000 = 600. Wetin dem go pay = 5,000 minus 600 = 4,400. Dem dey remove trade discount from the catalogue price before retailer go pay, as appreciation for buying from wholesaler.

q.q: Which of the following best describes a wholesaler in a channel of distribution?
options: A person who sells goods directly to final consumers in small units
A person who buys goods in large quantities from producers and sells them in smaller quantities to retailers
A person who sells goods directly to final consumers in small units at a fixed price
A government agent who collects import duty on goods
q.explanation: A wholesaler buys in bulk from manufacturers/producers and breaks the bulk into smaller quantities for retailers. This is the basic role of the wholesaler in the channel of distribution.
q.pidgin: Wholesaler na person wey dey buy plenty goods from producer, then e go break am small small sell am to retailer. Na im work be that for the distribution chain.
